Hello, Dolly! The nineteen sixty-four musical by Jerry Herman, music and lyrics, based on Thornton Wilder's play The Matchmaker. Set in turn-of-the-century New York, it follows Dolly Levi, a widowed matchmaker and schemer, as she attempts to make matches between wealthy merchant Horace Vandergelder and various women, while secretly pursuing him herself. The musical celebrates transformation, second chances, and the indomitable human spirit through infectious, jubilant songs and physical comedy.

Herman composed and wrote the entire score himself in a tour-de-force that won ten Tony Awards in nineteen sixty-four, including Best Musical. The title song "Hello, Dolly!" is one of musical theatre's most recognizable numbers, sung by Dolly at a restaurant, and instantly became a cultural phenomenon and jazz standard. Other celebrated songs include "Put On Your Sunday Clothes," "It Only Takes a Moment," "Before the Parade Passes By," and "Elegance."

The original production starred Carol Channing as Dolly, who won the Tony Award for Best Actress in a Musical. Later productions featured Pearl Bailey and Ethel Merman, all iconic. The plot is a sophisticated farce: Dolly returns to New York after several years, inserts herself into Horace's life, sabotages his planned marriage to another, and wins him for herself.

The show ran for twenty-eight hundred forty-four performances on Broadway from nineteen sixty-four to nineteen seventy, the longest-running show on Broadway at the time. The nineteen sixty-nine film featured Barbra Streisand. The musical is a celebration of theatrical spectacle and human resilience. Its central message—that life's best chapters come after loss and hardship—remains its emotional core.
